_comment: Which mod owns a Factorio subgroup's capability on Terra, and where known, which machine crafts it (#88).
Factorio's group/subgroup is its inventory shelf -- items sorted by what they are FOR. ADR-0017
assigns capabilities by the same axis, so the two taxonomies line up and a subgroup can name an
owner. A shelf is NOT a machine: `intermediate-product` holds a gear wheel, an advanced circuit
and a rocket fuel on one shelf.
TWO FIELDS, TWO AXES.
`owner`   -- whose capability this is, read off ADR-0017's table. Never invented here.
`process` -- the recipe type that crafts it, `mod:process`, present only where it is known.
A LIST where the recipe must be authored on more than one surface. Exactly two
rows are: `assembling-machine-1` and `automation-science-pack`, rung 1's
bootstrap pair -- the machine and the pack that buys it. A third is a finding.
They are not the same question and they routinely disagree. A Drilling Rig is GregTech's item
built in the pack's Assembling Machine, because ADR-0026 removed GT's Assembler and its corpus.
Create's belts are the same. Where they disagree, `cross_owner` says why -- and that field is the
point of the file, because a disagreement nobody wrote down is how `crafting` -> `assembling`
became wholesale in the first place. Where owner and machine ARE the same mod (`create:pressing`
on a gear wheel, `create:filling` on a barrel), the recipe is genuinely Create's end to end and
that is what keeps Create in series on the ladder rather than decorative.
Electro never yields an `electro:` process: the mod ships no machine, and its own recipes use
Create's `compacting`, `mixing`, `mechanical_crafting` and `sequenced_assembly` types in the
`electroenergetics` namespace. An owner with no machine of its own is not a contradiction.
THIS FILE ROUTES NOTHING. It is the guard rail `process-map.json` is checked against: every
emitted recipe's process must belong to the mod its subgroup names, and must equal `process`
where this file states one. That is what makes ADR-0017 a machine-checked invariant rather than
prose nobody re-reads. An unmapped recipe is still a hard failure, never a fallback to this file.
THE PERSONAL ASSEMBLER IS THE CRAFTING TABLE. The vanilla table and the equivalent grid blocks are
removed from the pack; the Personal Assembler replaces them rather than sitting beside them. So it is
not 'the grid' as distinct from a machine -- it is the pack's ONLY hand-crafting surface. #42's 'grid
recipes stay forbidden at every rung' is therefore moot rather than enforced: there is no other grid
left to forbid. Which blocks the removal takes, what it costs the two mods #45 screened clean, and the
player's un-removable 2x2 inventory grid are #90.
WHICH RECIPES IT CRAFTS IS A RULE, NOT A FIELD. Faithfully, almost everything that needs no fluid is
hand-craftable in Factorio, and marking that per recipe would be 113 annotations that all say the same
thing. The rule instead: THE PERSONAL ASSEMBLER CRAFTS WHAT ASSEMBLING MACHINE 1 CRAFTS -- every recipe
whose first category is `crafting`, and nothing else. `crafting-with-fluid` is excluded because the
surface has no tank, and `advanced-crafting` because Factorio itself withholds it from the hand. That
second exclusion is one recipe in the whole corpus, `engine-unit`, and it is the reason the rule is
phrased as machine 1's category set rather than as 'anything without a fluid': the two differ by
exactly that item, which takes no fluid and still may not be hand-made.
The rule is derived from `recipe.json` and asserted by the test, so NO ROW HERE NAMES THE PERSONAL
ASSEMBLER. It cannot: the predicate cuts across shelves rather than along them. 113 of the corpus's 163
recipes qualify, spread over 29 of the 34 shelves -- 24 wholly, and 5 (`intermediate-product`, `belt`,
`terrain`, `uranium-processing`, `space-interactors`) split down the middle. A shelf is the wrong
granularity for it, which is why it is not stored at all.
`owner` values: `gregtech`, `create`, `mekanism`, `electro`, `pack` (a machine this pack registers
on a GT chassis -- ADR-0025's Oil Refinery and Chemical Plant, ADR-0026's Assembling Machines),
`split` (the shelf straddles a seam; see `per_recipe`, written `owner / process` where the two
differ), `undecided` (ADR-0017 has no row for this capability -- a decision, not an oversight),
`deferred` (carved out to its own ticket; see `ticket`), `not_emitted` (out of the corpus's emit
scope; #87 owns that scope, this records why) and

logistics/belt.cross_owner: Create's belts, built in the pack's Assembling Machine. Create ships no machine that assembles a multi-part device; `mechanical_crafting` is a grid, not a machine, and Factorio builds belts in an assembler.

logistics/logistic-network.note: #28 gates Create 6's package logistics to the `logistic` rung; AE2 is endgame and not this shelf's answer.

logistics/train-transport.note: `rail-signal` and `rail-chain-signal` are circuit items on a Create shelf; they follow the shelf, not their ingredients.

note: A barrel is not fluid logistics. It is the opposite: it takes a fluid OFF the pipe network and
puts it on the belt, which is Factorio's own reason for the item. ADR-0017's fluid rows never
applied to it.
It is also the only assignment any installed mod can express. `create:filling` is the Spout;
Mekanism has no fluid-into-item recipe type at all (its Rotary Condensentrator is fluid to
chemical). Assigning this shelf to Mekanism repeated ADR-0017's own recorded mistake on the
Refining row -- an owner read off the capability table without checking the mod can express
the recipe.
Mekanism's part is the container, not the process: the Spout fills a Mekanism portable tank,
which carries far more per item than a vanilla bucket. Which container the eighteen `*-barrel`
items map to is #87's item map, not this file's routing.

intermediate-products/empty-barrel.note: `create:emptying`, the Item Drain. Same argument as `fill-barrel`.

production/extraction-machine.cross_owner: The one shelf GregTech still owns, and it does not craft its own machines: GT's stock Assembler and its whole corpus are removed (ADR-0026), so a Drilling Rig is built in the pack's Assembling Machine. Owner and machine differ here by design.
production/extraction-machine.note: `offshore-pump` and `pumpjack` are the fluid rig; the two mining drills are the ore ladder.

production/production-machine.reason: The shelf is uniformly the pack's: every machine on it is built in an Assembling Machine.
note: `assembling-machine-1` needed a hand surface or the ladder never starts -- the first Assembling
Machine cannot be built in an Assembling Machine. It no longer carries one as a field: the rule in
`_comment` gives it, because the recipe's category is `crafting`. The bootstrap is a CONSEQUENCE of
the rule now, not an exception carved out beside it, and that is the better shape -- an exception
would have needed defending every time the corpus was regenerated.
`centrifuge` is the machine that runs `centrifuging`, which is #89's chapter end to end -- deferred
with the chapter rather than assigned a build machine for a machine that may not ship.
Researchd's Research Lab replaces Factorio's `lab` (#45); the row stays so the item map has
something to point at.

intermediate-products/fluid-recipes.reason: Two oil-processing rows and seven chemistry rows; both are already one-to-one by category, so the qualifier is read off `category-map.json` rather than decided.
intermediate-products/fluid-recipes.adr_row: Oil processing / Chemistry / Refining -- the pack (ADR-0025)

intermediate-products/science-pack.reason: #26 keeps four rungs and drops the rest; the four that survive are Assembling Machine recipes.
note: THIS AMENDS #42, which reads `automation` is Personal Assembler only and 'stays there forever'. The
hand surface itself is no longer the amendment -- the rule in `_comment` grants it to every
`crafting` recipe, red science included. What is amended is the 'only': #42 forbids red science on
the Assembling Machine, and this row puts it there.
The argument is ADR-0021's fidelity axis. #42 was defending something real -- slow hand-crafting is
Factorio's own signature, and scaling it is why you want the Assembler -- and that holds for the
BOOTSTRAP and over-reaches past it. In Factorio red science is the canonical FIRST thing a player
automates; an assembling machine feeding a lab is the opening tutorial. Forbidding it on the machine
forbids the tutorial. What #42 actually protects is that rung 1 cannot REQUIRE the Assembler, and the
rule keeps that intact by construction.
#26's dropped Military and reserved Utility and Space make three of the seven `not_emitted`.
#42 also reads 'grid recipes for packs stay forbidden at every rung'. That clause is moot rather than
enforced: the vanilla crafting table and the equivalent grid blocks are REMOVED (#90), and the
Personal Assembler stands in their place. There is no third surface to forbid.

logistics/energy-pipe-distribution.reason: The shelf straddles ADR-0017's transmission/fluid-logistics seam -- Factorio files poles and pipes together because both carry stuff between machines; the pack does not.
logistics/energy-pipe-distribution.note: Written `owner / process`. Electro ships no machine of its own -- its own recipes use Create's `compacting`, `mixing`, `mechanical_crafting` and `sequenced_assembly` types in the `electroenergetics` namespace -- so an `electro` owner can never yield an `electro:` process.

logistics/storage.reason: ADR-0017 splits bulk storage by item vs fluid; Factorio does not.

production/energy.reason: ADR-0017's Power generation row is a three-way split (Create generates first, Mekanism at scale, Electro carries), half this shelf is the nuclear chapter, and the row's Create half does not survive contact with the mod -- see the note.
note: THE BOILER IS GREGTECH'S. #37 puts steam at rung 0, two machines wide -- LP Solid Boiler plus LP
Steam Miner -- so Factorio's `boiler` is GT's boiler, not a Create block. That is one of the two
things GregTech still does on Terra outside extraction, and it is why this row reads `gregtech`
rather than following ADR-0017's Power generation row.
`steam-engine` IS #92, AND IT REOPENS ADR-0017. That row reads 'Create generates first
(Steam Engine, rung 0)', but Create's Steam Engine emits ROTATIONAL FORCE, not FE. Factorio's
`steam-engine` is an electricity generator. So the two are not the same machine and the ADR names
an owner for a capability that mod cannot express -- the same failure ADR-0017 already recorded
against its own Refining row ('written without checking that Mekanism can express the recipe. It
cannot.'). What actually turns Terra's rung-0 steam into FE is an open question: Electro's
Alternator takes SU and emits watts and is called a generation SYSTEM in ADR-0017's own prose, but
it is explicitly not counted as generation in the table, and the grid is granted at a rung rather
than available at rung 0.
The four nuclear rows -- `heat-exchanger`, `heat-pipe`, `steam-turbine`, `nuclear-reactor` -- are
`deferred` to #89 with `intermediate-products/uranium-processing`: one chapter, one decision.
`steam-engine` is NOT among them: it is #92, Terra's first electricity generator.
production/energy.cross_owner: Every row here is an item of one mod built in the pack's Assembling Machine (ADR-0026); no owner on this shelf crafts its own machines.

production/smelting-machine.reason: The three furnaces are the machines that run `smelting`, and no ADR-0017 row owns smelting. Their build machine is `pack:assembling` like every other machine; what is undecided is which pack block each of Factorio's three tiers IS, which is #91 -- the same question as the plate rows in `intermediate-products/raw-material`.
production/smelting-machine.note: Previously `split-by-rung` on ADR-0017's Ore processing row -- the same misfiling as the plates; see that shelf's note. #42 names the Energized Smelter in the `production` pack's slot list, which is a data point for the furnace question and not an answer to it.
production/smelting-machine.cross_owner: The two questions come apart completely here. WHICH furnace these three map to is undecided -- ADR-0017 has no smelting row -- but whichever it is, a furnace is a machine and machines are built in the pack's Assembling Machine (ADR-0026). Settling the owner will not move the process.

intermediate-products/raw-material.reason: Four chemistry recipes and three smelting recipes on one shelf; the categories route them to different destinations.
note: FACTORIO SMELTS ORE STRAIGHT TO PLATE, and the pack does not get to add a step. All four
`smelting` recipes in the corpus are one hop -- `iron-ore` 1:1 to `iron-plate`, `copper-ore` 1:1 to
`copper-plate`, `steel-plate` from 5 iron plates, `stone-brick` from 2 stone. There is no ingot in
Factorio's chain at all: the PLATE is the base metal item, and an ore -> ingot -> plate ladder is a
Minecraft-mod idiom that ADR-0021's fidelity axis rules out.
These rows previously read `split-by-rung`, deferring to ADR-0017's Ore processing row (Create at
rung 0, Mekanism from rung 1). That was the wrong row. Ore PROCESSING in ADR-0017 means
multiplication -- crushing, enrichment, the 5x ladder -- and smelting is ore REDUCTION, which has
no rung structure. Reading one off the other turned three one-step recipes into a progression the
converter could not emit, which was an artefact of the misfiling and not a real problem.
`#69` (does the pack keep ore multiplication at all?) is therefore ORTHOGONAL to these rows, not
blocking them: it decides YIELD -- whether a side chain exists that turns 1 ore into more than 1
plate -- and never the shape or the destination of the smelting recipe itself. Nauvis has no ore
multiplication whatsoever, so the fidelity axis has an opinion there too, but that is #69's call.
What is still open is narrow and is a furnace, not a ladder: WHICH mod's smelter runs these four.
ADR-0017 has no smelting row -- `category-map.json` leaves `smelting.recipe_type` null for the same
reason -- so answering it ADDS a row to ADR-0017. That is #91; `undecided:smelting` retires with it.

intermediate-products/intermediate-produ.reason: The shelf that proves a subgroup is not a machine. Twelve recipes, four destinations, and the largest non-barrel `crafting` shelf in the corpus.
note: The four `create:pressing` rows are single-material forming -- one plate in, a shaped thing
out -- which is the Mechanical Press by shape, and the one place on this shelf where owner and
machine are the same mod. `processing-unit` takes 5x sulfuric acid and `rocket-fuel` takes
10x light oil, so both are Chemical Plant rather than Assembling Machine even though the owner
reads `pack` either way -- which is exactly why the qualifier exists. The circuit rows are
#55's authored three-tier ladder, not Factorio's items.

space/space-interactors.reason: The Rocket Silo is decided (#41); the cargo landing pad is the post-launch arc.
space/space-interactors.note: #41 makes the Rocket Part a cycle in a Rocket Silo multiblock rather than an item, 50 per launch. `rocket-building` is already one-to-one in `category-map.json`.

intermediate-products/uranium-processing.reason: Carved out to `Terra's uranium past the acid gate, and whether the nuclear chapter ships` (#89). #58 gives uranium's FIRST step an owner -- Factorio's sulfuric-acid gate as an authored `mekanism:dissolution` recipe at rung 3 -- but nothing owns enrichment, fuel cells or reprocessing, and ADR-0017 has no fission row to read one off.

logistics/circuit-network.reason: ADR-0017 has no row for a circuit network, and no installed mod owns one as a capability. #58 cut redstone from Terra entirely -- no vein, empty `underground_ores` step -- so the shelf's whole idiom has no source on the planet.
logistics/circuit-network.note: Eight recipes: five combinators, a power switch, a display panel, a programmable speaker, a small lamp. Most likely `not_emitted`, but that is a decision this table cannot take from ADR-0017.

logistics/terrain.reason: ADR-0017 has no terrain row. `concrete` is stone brick plus water, which is `create:mixing` by shape, but nothing in the table says Create owns terrain.
logistics/terrain.note: Six recipes: concrete, refined concrete, the two hazard variants, landfill, stone-brick. `stone-brick` is `smelting` -- 2 stone to 1 brick, one step -- and follows the furnace question in `intermediate-products/raw-material`, NOT ADR-0017's Ore processing row; it was briefly filed there by the same error. Landfill has no meaning on a flat, sea-bearing Terra (ADR-0019) and may be the clearest cut on this shelf.

logistics/transport.reason: One recipe, `car`. Personal transport is not an ADR-0017 capability and no rung grants it.

production/module.reason: One recipe, `beacon`. Factorio's module system has no pack analogue; #42 names a Mekanism upgrade in the `production` pack's slot list, which is the nearest thing and is not this.

production/tool.reason: One recipe, `repair-pack`. Nothing on Terra takes damage the way a Factorio entity does.

combat/ammo.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/armor.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/capsule.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/equipment.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/gun.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/turret.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/utility-equipment.reason: #26 dropped Military science -- its ingredients feed nothing downstream.

combat/defensive-structure.note: Contains `radar`. #57 decided a continuous FE Radar as a `gtceu:machine` KubeJS registration with the mechanism in `planetaryfactory_core`, unlocked by its own research node -- a pack machine, not Factorio's item, so this row stays cut and the Radar is authored rather than converted.

space/space-crushing.reason: Map #25 Out of scope -- Space Science and the asteroid economy are the next arc, past the destination. Already `!asteroids-are-post-launch` in `category-map.json`.
